title: 2100 S. Prairie Avenue
camera_position: from the northeast, at the Prairie Avenue / 21st Street intersection (house stands at the SW corner of Prairie and 21st per Sullivan, quoted on Glessner blog); north (21st Street) flank receding at right
creator: unknown photographer
repository: Chicagology (chicagology.com) — website compilation; original holder not credited on page
rights_basis: Website reproduction without credited source or rights statement; original holder and rights unresolved
notes: High-quality albumen-era photograph of the Burnham & Root Sherman house (completed 1876): two-and-a-half storeys of dark brick banded with light stone over a high rusticated stone basement, steep slate roofs with Gothic gabled dormers and iron cresting, a tall corner pavilion with conical/hipped slate roof and finial, carved chimney stacks, a front porch carried on clustered colonnettes reached by a curved stone stair with pierced balustrade, a side bay/oriel on the 21st Street flank, low stone-post-and-iron front fence, parkway trees, plank-guard tree boxes and stone sidewalk. A woman stands on the porch; two children sit at the curb. A numeral '4' is printed lower right (plate/series number). Chicagology gives no source; the CHM holds ICHi-001299 'Sherman house, 2100 Prairie, circa 1890' (marker credit) which may be this or a related view — unverified. Key reference for the 1904 massing; the house stood until 1936 so 1904 appearance should match unless altered after the photo. The same photograph is reproduced on the Glessner House blog ('Prairie Avenue and Louis Sullivan – Part I', 2020-06-02), which quotes Sullivan's Autobiography of an Idea describing the house 'nearing completion' on the SW corner of Prairie and 21st.

notes: Line engraving of the Henry S. Jaffray-designed Hanford house (1883): massive two-and-a-half/three-storey ashlar (Connecticut brownstone per blog) block with a steep pyramidal/hipped slate roof, tall dormers with gables and finials, an oriel on the side, bay windows, a corner entrance porch with columns and balustraded deck reached by a long stone stair. The blog: largest house on Calumet; vacant for decades after Hanford's 1893 suicide; fire-damaged; demolished 1953. In 1904 the house was standing but unoccupied (caretaker) per blog.

notes: Entrance of the Calvin T. Wheeler house (Otis L. Wheelock, 1870; Kohn family from 1874): red brick with stone-trimmed round-arched windows with keyed hoods, gabled wooden/stone entry porch with pierced brackets and colonnettes, stone stair with pierced (circle-pattern) balustrade and urn. Blog gives address as 2020 S. Calumet, Second Empire style, Kohn family sold early 1900s → publishing company offices → Murphy Butter & Egg warehouse (loading dock around dining room) → restored 1997–99 as Wheeler Mansion hotel. Also interior photos (vestibule mosaic, Lincrusta ceilings, hall, dining room) in the same post. Note: the house was MOVED — verify (the City landmark report should say) whether 2020 is its original 1904 site.
